title: Kingdom Keys To Insulating Yourself In Times of Crisis
paragraphs: In other words, I want to focus in this session on discovering your real work outside of your job. Typically, what economic crises do is affect your job. I think one of the first signs that we were heading towards a recession was the downsizing and bankruptcies of companies, and also the collapse of huge corporations. People are starting to lose their jobs. That is a sign of an economic crisis.

There are different types of crises, but the crisis we are dealing with in the world now, which they say will last for about 5 years, is an economic crisis. Now, the economic crisis is not isolated from all the other crises that it will cause. For example, an economic crisis will produce a crisis in national depression. The countries will become depressed. This is when they actually feel concerned globally because a depression is worse than a recession. Recession is the effect of events on the economy.

A depression is when the psyche of a nation turns negative, and that's when people start to lose hope, and you do n't want to reach that stage. Now, what leads to a recession is stagnation. People begin to feel hopeless. They begin to despair. That's because they cannot control their lives. Banks have taken over their lives. Certain companies seize their physical assets, and they feel completely helpless. This is where people start to think about another crisis, which is suicide.

Suicide rates rise during recessions. Another crisis resulting from the economic recession is family breakdown. This is when divorce rates increase and domestic violence increases. This is when abuse occurs within the home. This is when people start to feel frustrated within their families and begin to hurt each other because they cannot control their situation. This leads to another crisis, which is crime.

When people cannot find food because they cannot find money due to a lack of jobs, they try to earn a living in the best way they can. Some people resort to antisocial activities, which we call criminal activities. This is the time when drug sales, illegal drug sales, rise, because people start getting into it. They leave the legal market because they cannot find work, and enter the illegal market to try to survive.

This is where people begin to sacrifice their integrity, character, and self-respect just to earn a living. Also, believe me or not, there is also a crisis in subcultures such as prostitution. The number of people working in prostitution is increasing because people are starting to sell their bodies even to make a living. This means we are not talking about just one crisis here. Rather, it has a cascading effect. The other crisis that will result from this, of course, is that people will begin to deal with fear.

You find people locking their doors and guarding their property, and people starting to buy more weapons, because when people feel threatened by others who may have nothing, they try to defend themselves. So you can see that this crisis should not be underestimated. This could escalate into a very dangerous environment for all of us. Let me now give you a definition of a crisis. I have a picture here of a hurricane, or what we call a hurricane in the Bahamas.

In some parts of the United States, what exactly do they call it? A funnel cloud. A tropical cyclone is actually a massive funnel cloud. But look at this picture over there. You see a beautiful path leading towards danger. And now, here you are driving your car on this road and a tropical cyclone or funnel cloud is heading towards you. In the Far East, they call it a tropical cyclone. What can you do? You didn't start it. You can't stop it. You didn't cause it to happen. So, this is how we define what a crisis is.

Please note that. A crisis is an event, circumstance, or situation that affects you or your environment, and for which you have no direct cause, control, or responsibility. This is extremely important. The crisis is something you did not cause. You cannot control it. You cannot take responsibility for that or blame anyone else for it. Incidentally, this is extremely dangerous because these are the times when politicians become very active.

They begin to blame their political opponents for problems they did not cause themselves. This is the time when many politicians try to score political points. But the crisis is not caused by the actions of any one person. Rather, it is a meeting point of many different parts. We have faced economic challenges before. But it never affected us globally or nationally. We have gone through periods in our history not so long ago; in 1982 there was an economic crisis.

We have seen oil and gasoline prices rise several times over the past ten years. But that did not affect the nation as a whole. A crisis is the result of different paths of events converging at one time and in one place. And that's exactly what happened. And so we have something that we cannot control. I will write this down. Also, you are always in control of your mindset. And your ideas. And your mind. You also always control your perception of what is happening. You cannot control a hurricane.

You cannot control the storm. You cannot control the whirlwind. You cannot control what we call a crisis. But what you can control is how you think about it. The word "concept" is extremely important here. Whatever you can imagine, it is extremely important. I have heard this phrase many times before. You can turn a small hill into a mountain, and this happens inside your head. And most of us live that way. We live based more on what we think than on reality. So here's a phrase I want you to remember.

The power of your thoughts and words. When you enter a crisis environment, you must be very careful in controlling your thoughts and words. First, this relates to the power of your thoughts and words. First, whatever you name or describe becomes your reality. Whatever you name or describe becomes your reality. I cannot stress enough how important this is because you control the labels you give to things. For example, you call your shoe a shoe and treat it as a shoe, but I might call it the hide of a dead cow.

This platform that I am standing on, you call it a platform. They are actually petroleum derivatives. Reinforced plastic. Whatever you call it, that's what it represents to you. Secondly, everything that something represents to you controls your response to it. That's why what you call it is so important. You determine your behavior in life through how you categorize things. This is true about everything in life. Whatever you name something controls your response to it.

I remember Jesus Christ when he faced a crisis once. He had a very close friend. In fact, one of his best friends was named Lazarus. Lazarus actually lived in a house that Jesus used to visit whenever he went to that town. He ate and slept there many times. You remember the story when he was in another city and someone sent him a message that Lazarus was sick. You may find that Jesus' words continued to contradict their messages. They kept sending him these messages. One of the messages said that Lazarus was sick.

Jesus says that this illness is not fatal. Then they said that Lazarus's condition had worsened. He said he would be fine. Then they said that Lazarus was dying. He says he'll be fine. Then they sent the final message that Lazarus had died. Jesus said that he was not dead. He is asleep. Now, why is this important? They said he died. He used a different term. He is asleep. If someone dies, you really can't wake them up. But if you say that someone is asleep, you have changed your response towards that person.

What he was really dealing with was trying to teach us how to speak, and how to think. So his response was that he was asleep, and then he said, "Let's go and wake him up." That's what he said after that. And now you know that his response is, " Let's go," because what I call it is what it is. What do you call losing your job? Unemployed?

Well, if you feel unemployed, your response will be: I do n't have a job, which means I don't have a source of income, which means I can't manage my life, which therefore means I'm depressed, and therefore my response to life is to give up. But you could call losing a job something completely different, as the Japanese do. The word for crisis in Japanese and Chinese means opportunity. So when you fire a Chinese person, he calls it an opportunity. Now, if something is an opportunity, then you take advantage of it.

Don't let him take advantage of you. Did you see? So, what you call things controls your response to them. Number three, disciplined perception is not a denial of reality. This is very important. Disciplined perception is not a denial of reality, but rather control over one's response to reality. This is extremely important. We are not going around saying there is no economic crisis, no one is losing their job, and everything is fine. We don't say that.

What we are saying is that our interpretation of this matter is different. Our perspective on this matter comes from a different culture. We are from the culture of the Kingdom. For example, the Apostle Paul lived a very quiet and disciplined life, and this discipline stemmed from his way of perceiving everything. Let me quote one of his sayings that I love. Paul says, "All things work together for good." Now, how can you disappoint a man who has this perspective? What does he say?

All things work together for good because I am what? He says, "Because I am loved and called according to God's purpose." This means that I was sent to Earth on a mission, and whoever sent me controls everything, including the hurricane. Amen. You know, there are two animals in the Bible that God associates with himself. I think one of them would be good to remember now, and that's the eagle. Eagles are amazing creatures. When an eagle sees a storm in the desert, it actually flies towards it. Why?

Because the eagle is the only bird that uses the storm to rest. Why? Because the wind currents in the storm lift the eagles upwards, they use them to soar and rest for hours. He's simply riding the storm. You sometimes read in the Bible that God rides the storm. This means that when you are in the kingdom of God, you interpret the storm as an opportunity to rise to a higher level. It's about how you perceive things.

Therefore, my understanding is that nothing bad can happen to me, because the bad in my kingdom is controlled by a good God. Is there anyone who wants to say "Amen" alone? Therefore, there is no evil in the kingdom of God. If you put me into a furnace of fire, it will make me unburnable like Shadrach. If he puts me in the lions' den, he gives me a soft pillow to lie on. It just depends on where you live. If you are in the kingdom of God, even crucifixion turns into victory. Yes. Amen. You use death to kill death.

Your perception is what controls your response. Number four, a crisis is simply a change in the environment that requires a new and unscheduled response. This is a very important statement. I'll say it again. A crisis is simply a change in the environment one is accustomed to. It changes the familiar environment and requires a response that you hadn't planned for. For example, you have habits in your life that control you.

You go to work in the morning, return home in the evening, perform certain tasks, receive your salary at the end of the week or the end of the month, use your money to do this and that, and you have this kind of life schedule that you follow. Then a crisis comes. Boom. And you lose your job. Now wait a moment. I still have to wake up on Monday morning. But the way I used to schedule my life has changed. Therefore, I must respond differently. I didn't plan to respond this way. I'm not used to this.

Therefore, I must learn a new way of responding. This is what crises do. The crisis is good. That's exactly right, because the crisis—as I mentioned to you in the previous session—is a very important statement. I hope you wrote it down on Sunday. good. The crisis is bringing about the end of traditions. I'll say it again. The crisis is ending traditions. There are things I've become so accustomed to doing that only a crisis can break them.

What is happening now is that the whole world today, as you know, has been living on traditional institutional policies and programs. For example, I was speaking with a government minister today, a very important minister in our government who is concerned with the economy, and I said to him: As you know, I will send you the lesson I gave on Sunday. He said: Please. He said: I have heard about him. Call to get a copy. I said: Yes. I said: Do you know why I'm going to send it to you?

I said this because what our country and all countries are going through is the destruction of everything I obtained a university degree in. Yes. Think about it. You have a degree in economics. Guess what? It is completely useless because all the principles in your college economics books have faded away, because those are the principles that they actually say caused the problem. So now we need to rewrite the books, and rewrite the technical methods of life. In other words, the crisis requires a new response.

What you were doing previously is no longer effective. Number four, or rather five. Crisis is a source of creativity. This is why we must find new ways to respond to life. I am saying this to you to give you encouragement. Do not become depressed and do not listen to the negative talk around you. You need to adjust your perspective on this matter from the Kingdom's point of view. You belong to the Kingdom of Heaven. You may be living on Earth right now, but your government is living inside you too.

Your outlook on life should come from another culture. And the culture of Heaven is that no harm can befall me. So I have to find the positive side of this. I am supposed to take advantage of this crisis. Say Amen. The crisis is not meant to destroy me, but rather to lift me up like an eagle through it. You know, if you study biblical figures, you'll find that they were all promoted after a crisis. Let's take Daniel as an example.

Daniel was a secretary in the government, and when he came out unharmed from the lions' den, they appointed him a minister, i. e. , deputy prime minister. Joseph was a slave. When he was released from prison and explained the crisis to Pharaoh, he became Deputy Prime Minister. Esther, when her people were on the verge of annihilation, took a risk and stepped into the middle of the crisis in front of the king and became queen. Does anyone here want to get promoted? Your crisis is God's program for your advancement.

Say Amen if you need to understand that. Just say: Lord, yes. Say yes. Say yes. In other words, God doesn't want you to panic. Rather, he wants you to plan for advancement. So, how should you think? In a creative way. You need to think differently. That's why we must be careful about what we say. Here are some phrases I found very important to remind you of, and how important it is to say the right thing at the right time. The power of words.

First, Proverbs 18:21 says: “Death and life are in the hand of the tongue. Whoever loves to use their tongue wrongly will eat its fruit.” Death and life are in the power of the tongue. In other words, death and life are not in the surrounding environment. Lisa is not in the circumstances. Lisa is not involved in the events we are going through. Lisa is in crisis. Rather, it's in what you say about this situation. Oh God, I will not be able to survive. Oh Lord, what am I to do now? Lord, nothing will help me now.

Oh God, everything is falling apart. Oh my God, how am I going to manage until the end of the month? Lord, my house is not big enough. Ah, and you keep talking. Note that he says: "You will eat from the fruit of that." It is amazing that when God created the heavens and the earth, He made everything beautiful. If you read the second verse of Genesis in the Bible, it says: " The earth was formless and empty, and darkness was over the surface of the deep." So something went wrong in God's creation.

It is believed that in the second verse, Satan was expelled from heaven and brought chaos to this planet. But in the third verse, the book says that the Lord looked into the darkness. And you know that everything God says comes true. God refused to say, "It is dark." Because if he had said what he saw. Should I repeat it again? If he had said what he saw, he would have gotten what he said. God did not deny the reality of darkness. Instead, he preferred to say what he wanted to say. I will say Amen to myself.

I'll say it again. God did not deny the reality of darkness. But he refused to admit or say what he had seen. He preferred to say what he wished. He got what he wished for. He said, "Let there be light," and there was light. So you must be careful with your words. Secondly, Proverbs 11:9 says: “ With the mouth a hypocrite destroys his neighbor.” This means you keep talking about everyone getting fired from their jobs. You must be careful. You will not succeed in that.

You're just going to make it difficult for all of us. Boy, we will never survive this. You will lose your home, your car, your dog, and even your recording device. Do you know anything, man? You will get sick. Your marriage will fall apart, man. And that's how that neighbor destroys you with his words. This is the right time to stay away from negative people. Because they have a lot of material now. They don't have to manufacture anything. They have enough.

The news comes every day on a silver platter and they want to serve it to you. Tell your neighbor: "You will emerge from this crisis with a resounding victory." Tell your neighbor: "Everything will fall off you like water falls off a duck's feathers." Go ahead, say it. Tell your neighbor: " You will be completely protected from this crisis." So there's no need to panic. Make some plans. Tell your neighbor: "There is life after the test." So I'll see you on the other side of this test.

Give God a round of applause for the positive neighbors. You see, this is what we need. But through knowledge, the righteous survive. Look at the following phrase. With his mouth, the wicked destroy his neighbor. But with knowledge. Let everyone speak up. Knowledge means that there is something you know that your neighbor does not know. So don't listen to what your neighbor says. Tell them what you know. I remember we talked about this in our last meeting on Sunday. Jesus said, " I will give you secrets.

The secrets of the kingdom will be given to you." This means you have knowledge that the general public does not have. He says: "Now speak knowledge, not of what you see, but of what you know." What you see exists, but you speak what you know. This cannot destroy me. I am stronger than this. I am made of steel in the kingdom. Every machine made against me will fail. I am victorious. My Savior has overcome the world. Therefore, I will overcome this too. You should speak about what you know, not what you see.

Because what you see, if you speak of what you see, you will get more of it. No, you know, the Bible does use some contradictory phrases like these. Let the weak say, let the weak say that he is strong. What should the weak say? I am strong. The Bible says: "Let the poor man say, ' What? I am rich.'" So, you don't deny that you don't have money, you know that. But you don't have to say that. You have to say, I am rich. Why? I'm temporarily broke. Praise God for the temporary circumstances. any. Hallelujah.

So, victory is in the mouth, not in the eyes. Yes. Amen. Here is another verse that I thought was important to remember. Proverbs 11, he says, and this is very important for the country. Now, every country, by the blessing of the upright, the city is raised up, and by the mouth of the wicked, it is brought down. You have never seen this verse before. God says, " Look, the country will become what whoever speaks the loudest says." Say, "You can destroy a city with your mouth." " Look at that verse."

This means we need people in the public sphere, whether in politics, service, business, education, or employment. We need people who can say the things we want to see happen, not what we see with our own eyes. You can destroy an entire city with your mouth. So the bad guys say things like, "We'll never get over this." "Hmm-Half the country is going to hell." You know, maybe you should prepare to leave, and they start with all these expectations and expectations and expectations.

Oh, do you realize that you don't have to say everything you see? The book says that you can destroy an entire country with your mouth. So, what do the friends do? They are blessing the city. The Bahamas is where God lives. Therefore, we are protected. Thank God. A thousand falls to our right, whatever that country may be. And thousands more, ten thousand on the left, whatever that country may be, but it will not come near our country. It's better to take care of your own country. Amen. Yes.

The power of negative advertising, the power of negative statements made by a leader in a country, can destroy that country. That's why true leaders never promote discouragement. Let's go. They do not spread depression. They always speak with hope. Hope. Because hope gives the whole country hope. When you speak with hope, it is because God is the God of hope. The Bible says, say, say to yourself, I am more than enough. I'm more for any situation. Tell your neighbor, I have what I need.

I have what it takes to deal with anything, including my own country. Tell your neighbor, my country is about to be upgraded. You can destroy a city with your mouth. The power of your words. Now, let me give you what I call the power of response. This phrase has stayed with me for years. What happens to you is not what matters. But what you do in response to what happens to you is what really matters. In other words, the response is more important than the experience. This is correct.

We are going through some things. Okay, that's acceptable. But how will we respond to what we are going through? Your response is more important than the experience itself. Therefore, we need to focus on our response as individuals, as a society, and as a country, rather than describing the situation. We are aware of the situation. We know what they expect, but our response is more important than what they predict. So, what happens to us isn't really important. So, what are we going to do about it?

Here's something I want you to remember, this phrase. Doing nothing is not an option. Say it with me. Let me tell you something. You can't just sit and wait for this to pass. You'd better do something. Do n't wait for anyone to bring you anything. You know, don't sit around praying, expecting God to drop something from the ceiling. It's better if you go out and get to work. If you are in the kingdom of God, you must be proactive.

And by the way, I want to encourage you to stop being a consumer, because that's what's killing us, and start being a producer. We need to stop playing the victim and start creating victories. Doing nothing is not an option. Therefore, you must respond and do so effectively. Now, here are some things I want to remember, and I read this recently and it really made me happy. These are the words of the young man who liberated the entire nation of India. He was only 4 feet 2 inches tall. He weighed about 97 pounds.

His name is Mahatma Gandhi. His vision and faith in his country were amazing. He destroyed the entire British army with just his stance. The strength of the position. His position was so strong and deadly that he disarmed the entire British army. Here's what he says will destroy humanity. I want you to write it down because you will see how true his words are. Keep in mind that all of this is found in the holy books. First, he says politics without principles. This is the first one. This will destroy people.

Oh my God, that's true. In every country. Secondly, pleasure without conscience. wow. That's why we have AIDS. We are celebrating AIDS Week this week and everyone is talking about it. You know, I heard a young man on TV tonight and they were talking about his story. He said, "You know, man, I didn't realize I might have AIDS." He said, " But I was enjoying myself. I was sexually active." Well, the result is death. A country becomes corrupt when people indulge in pleasures without conscience.

Even issues related to alternative lifestyles, and that's what we want. This is what we want to do. We as countries must be careful to question what our conscience tells us. I am talking about the national conscience, not just your personal conscience. This is what destroyed Rome. Rome is the greatest country in history. It has never been destroyed by any army. Immorality has destroyed it. Pleasures destroyed Rome. Third, wealth without work. Man, this is a big problem for the Caribbean.

He says: "Nothing can destroy a country faster than people who want to get rich but don't want to work." You will never hear anyone say, 'Ah, I came to work, but don't give me any work.' This is the reason for the country's poverty. This is why the country has never been able to progress. Wealth without work will destroy any nation. Fourth, knowledge without ethics. People who have education, but lack the character to manage that education. They use knowledge to destroy people.

Fifth, and I have highlighted this, is trade without ethics. This is what they say was the cause of the crisis. Businessmen who lacked morals. Sixth, science without humanity. You know, they're talking about using embryos to produce stem cells for growing organs in adults. Basically, the whole idea is to take an embryo, a living baby embryo, and use its cells to produce organs. So, you are destroying a small child to create cells for other people's organs.

This is a science that requires us to question our humanity. What about abortion? Yes, we have the science to remove a child from a woman's womb because it causes her discomfort. But should we question the humanity of that? Is this considered murder? These are very important questions for us, and we must address them when we talk about the crisis. We have become victims of crises that we impose on our countries and on our private lives.

So, what I want to talk about in this last part is: how do you respond to the dilemmas of a crisis? First and foremost, let me tell you that your future is not in your job. Can you write that down somewhere? There is no future in any job. Think beyond your job. Say that with me. Think beyond your job. You know, I was in Orlando, Florida last week, and my friend there lives in a gated residential complex. The homes there range in price from $500,000 to $800,000 to $1 million.

One of them was worth one million eight hundred thousand dollars. I mean, this kind of upscale neighborhood. We were having dinner with them in that walled compound. He told me, "Dr. Monroe, you wouldn't believe how many people here in this community are losing their homes one by one." He said: "Their portfolios collapsed in the stock market in one day and they went from millionaires to paupers." I said, "This cannot be true." He said, "I'll take you for a walk."

After we had eaten, he took my wife and me on a tour around the entire neighborhood. He was only counting: one, two, for sale, for sale, for sale, mortgage, mortgage, two million dollars, five million dollars. I mean 800,000, 500,000. He told me that they all left in one day. They lost their jobs. All their assets evaporated. All their cash reserves disappeared. How do you explain to your five- year-old that you moved from a two-million- dollar house to an apartment in one week? That is the crisis.

So please write this down. There is no future in any job. Why? The future lies with the person who occupies the job. We all go up escalators in life. And some of us go down. I do n't know which way you're going. But in this life you either go up or down. You are in constant motion. No one stands still. Therefore, you need to determine where you stand on this escalator in life and what you will do about your movement. If you are descending, you have to make decisions to move to the other ladder.

If you are going up, you need to make sure you do some things to ensure that you don't end up on the other side of the staircase because it's going down. You are not safe if you currently have a job. That's the truth. Ask those who have lost her. They will tell you that. Some of them spent 20 or 30 years in their jobs. Seniority does not provide security in times of crisis. And by the way, your university degree does not provide security in times of crisis.

I know you have a PhD, but we simply cannot afford your salary. In fact, you cost us more than a bachelor's degree holder. Therefore, we will dispense with the PhD holder and keep the Bachelor's degree holder. So, even if you go around saying, "Well, I'm educated." That could be your curse. Okay. There is no future in the job. Where does the future lie? In the person who occupies the job. What I want to do is shift your expectations from external dependence to an internal awareness of your identity.

Actually, write this down. You have to create your own business within your job. When you go to work tomorrow, I want to encourage you to work harder than you have ever worked before and make yourself indispensable. In other words, a job does not protect you. You protect the job through the way you work. Now, let me tell you what I mean by that. Most companies are very happy about this crisis. Use your imagination.

They have been trying to get rid of you for a long time and have not been able to find a legitimate reason. The first person they always get rid of is the least productive or the one who has provided the least value to the work. Okay. So, the way you protect yourself now is to add value. Actually, please write this down. Make yourself indispensable by improving your value at work. This means going to work early. Do things they didn't ask you to do. Come up with ideas to develop the company.

I mean, produce like never before. Solve the problems they cannot solve. Devise ways to make them richer, and they will stay with you. But if you sit at work complaining, feeling frustrated, criticizing the company and wondering why they do that, you'll be the first one they get rid of when things fall apart. There are some people who will not be laid off. I'm telling you this now because they've kept their jobs for the past two or three years. They were productive. They were hardworking. They were creative.

They were contributing to the company. They were making it valuable. They weren't working just for money. This is correct. They are the ones we will keep. Therefore, it is best to change within 24 hours. Right now, I'm telling you, this is not the time to arrive at work five minutes before nine and walk around as if you just had breakfast. You need to arrive at work at 8:30, don't be late. Do n't leave. Listen, if you leave work now at five, you're finished.

This is not the time to work overtime and then demand extra pay. They are already paying you. They are paying your salary now. So don't talk about extra time. In other words, your attitude must change immediately in the midst of the crisis. You should be like Daniel. Daniel was very distinguished in his work. The text says that King Nebuchadnezzar promoted him. He expelled all the other people around him.

But Daniel's distinction in action was that he did not say that it was his time of prayer that impressed the king or that he placed the Bible on the desk. Daniel's outstanding work was what protected his job. You need to improve your value at work. This is how you survive the crisis. Ah, you know, Joseph was promoted during the crisis because he provided value to the king's court. When the king told his dream to all the dream interpreters, none of them could interpret it. Do you remember that story?

Then he says that the baker said: "There is a man I met in prison who accurately interpreted my dream." The king says, "Go and bring him." Let me tell you something. When you provide value to any organization, they will find you even in the closet and bring you to the head office. Crises give you the opportunity to hone your talent. Let me remind you of a few things. Your job versus your work. This is extremely important. Number one. Never confuse your work with your job. Repeat after me.

You know that this needs to be said to everyone in this country right now. More than one million people have already lost their jobs in the United States. This may not seem like a large number, but it is a large number of people. There is a possibility that 5 million or more people could lose their jobs if car companies collapse. This affects the Bahamas immediately because we depend on external resources to survive. Therefore, we should talk about jobs. Never confuse your job with your work.

Number two, your job is what you were trained to do. That's why they can kick you out. But your job is what you were born to do. They cannot expel that. You need to change your way of thinking now. Instead of waiting to find a job, try to find yourself. The book I mentioned to you at the beginning is an important book. Please take some time to read it.

I spent perhaps, I estimate, 25 years writing that book, because it required 25 years of trying to understand life, and finally I think I have grasped its essence, and I am living proof of that; It means: When you find your real job, they can never threaten you with losing your job. Let's go. Actually, here's number three, or rather, number four. Your job is your career. You can lose your career, but your job is your purpose in life. They cannot take that away from you.

You know, you can chase a bird off your balcony, but you can't take away its ability to fly. Whatever you were born to do, you were born with the talent for it. So they may move you from place to place or kick you out, but you carry your truth with you wherever you go. Your worth should lie in who you are, not in what they ask you to do. In fact, number six, your job is your skills. And by the way, let me just say this. This is extremely dangerous here. Skills.

In times of crisis, your skills may become completely useless. For example, here you are. You are a carpenter, but the construction sector is at a standstill. So now your skill is useless. You need to learn new skills. They actually call this rehabilitating yourself, reinventing yourself. And here you are in this situation. You know, you were working as a waiter.
